Durability is a property of what the *next* `Open` can reconstruct; a same-handle observation cannot witness it by construction.\n\n## 4. Smallest repair principle and a regression test (described, not implemented)\n\n**Repair principle — restore the invariant the `flush()` guard depends on:** after WAL replay, the segment must again own a live WAL handle reflecting its unpersisted memory state. Concretely, at the end of `SegmentImpl::recover()` (or in `Open` right after it, `segment.cc:500`), when a WAL file existed, call the existing `open_wal_file()` (`segment.cc:4303-4322`). It opens the existing file with `create_new = false`, and `LocalWalFile::open` seeks to the end for appending (`local_wal_file.cc:92-106`), so `wal_file_ != nullptr` and `has_record()` is true again. Then `dump()`/`flush()`/`Optimize()` — and also a plain `Collection::Flush()`, which is a no-op today for the same reason (`collection.cc:389-395`) — take the full path: persist memory components, register persisted blocks in the meta, update the version, and remove the WAL only after the data is durable. A deeper alternative (make the guard test unpersisted memory state, e.g. `memory_store_ != nullptr` or writing-block `doc_count_ != 0`, instead of the WAL handle) also works but changes more semantics; handle re-attachment is the minimal fix.\n\n**Regression test** — fits the existing crash-recovery harness (`tests/db/crash_recovery/write_recovery_test.cc:56-148`: fork/exec a data-generator child, `SIGKILL` to simulate the crash; `CreateTestSchema` in `tests/db/crash_recovery/utility.h:38-65` sets `max_doc_count_per_segment = 10000`):\n\n1. Child process: create+open the collection, insert N docs (N small, e.g. a few hundred — far below rollover thresholds), then die abruptly *before* any flush or clean shutdown (SIGKILL after the inserts, or `_exit()` to bypass destructors).\n2. Parent: `Collection::Open` (triggers WAL replay); record `c = Stats().doc_count` and assert `c == N` and that fetch-by-pk returns all docs (recovery baseline).\n3. Call `Optimize()`; assert OK.\n4. Assert same-handle `Stats().doc_count == c` (documents the \"looks healthy\" phase).\n5. **Release the handle and `Open` again; assert `doc_count == c` and every pk fetches.** This is the assertion that fails on the current code (count 0) and must pass after the repair — it is the only step that distinguishes \"optimize succeeded\" from \"optimize preserved recovered data.\"\n6. Optional white-box checks: after the repair, no `*.wal` file remains under the collection directory (the fixed flush removes it at `segment.cc:2304-2315`), and the manifest lists a persisted forward block for the sealed segment.\n7. Keep a control test: identical sequence without the crash between insert and `Optimize` — passes before and after, isolating the recovery-specific regression.\n\nTo avoid SIGKILL-timing nondeterminism, the child can run the generator to completion in a \"no clean shutdown\" mode, or the test can simply capture whatever count survived the crash (assert `c > 0`) and carry that same `c` through steps 3-5.\n\n## Established from source vs. requiring execution\n\nEverything above is from static reading of the frozen tree — I did not build or run anything, and I am not claiming a reproduction.
